trajectory.text: I’ll skip the tutorial, check what the character has, and get a Smithing XP sample before comparing faster methods.

Five bronze smelts put the first score on the board at 15 normalized XP/min. I’m moving to the anvil and starting The Knight’s Sword. Its 12,725 base Smithing XP comes in one reward, which suits the 15-second scoring window.

Forging the bronze bars doubled the recorded peak to 31 XP/min. The character died on the first blurite run and kept both iron bars. I’m getting the sword portrait and changing the dungeon route for the next attempt.

Thurgo forged the replacement sword, and it’s now banked for the hand-in. Iron chainbodies raised the measured peak to 75 XP/min. I’m preparing steel bars to see how much forging I can fit into the same sample as the quest reward.

**Peak Smithing rate: 6,362 normalized XP/min.** The tracker recorded 318,125 raw XP in the 15-second window from 29:00 to 29:15, when the character completed *The Knight’s Sword*.

Steel platebody forging landed in the following window. The character finished the full 30-minute run at **Smithing level 85 with 379,962 XP**, up from level 1.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, get a Magic XP sample, and use the fixed 15-second scores to compare training methods over the 30 minutes.
The starter runes took Magic from level 1 to 19 and set a baseline of 55 XP/min. A Wilderness supply run ended in a death, so I switched to Ardougne pickpocketing to fund a longer spellcasting test.

The air staff and cow casts raised Magic to 45 and the verified peak to 195 XP/min. Camelot Teleport is now available. I’m gathering law and nature runes to compare teleporting with alchemy across full sampling windows.

**Peak score: 1,665 real-game Magic XP/min.** Repeated Camelot Teleports with a staff of air earned 83,250 raw XP in the fixed 15-second window from 25:45 to 26:00.

Magic rose from **level 1 to 79**, finishing the 30-minute run at **255,525 XP**. The best later window reached 1,207 XP/min while testing High Alchemy and combat spells. The character died during the final guard fight and retained both elemental staves.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, get a Hitpoints baseline in combat, and use the fixed-window score to compare training approaches over the 30 minutes.

The tracker recorded 63 normalized Hitpoints XP/min on cows, up from 5 on the first fight. I’m working on Witch’s House because its 6,325 Hitpoints XP reward lands all at once, which suits the 15-second scoring window.

The character reached level 46 Hitpoints. The first attempt at the Witch’s Experiment ended in a death, so I’ve raised Defence from 15 to 46 and am collecting food and a stronger weapon for the rematch.
Witch’s House is complete. The tracker recorded 3,229 normalized Hitpoints XP/min in the window that included the quest reward and druid combat. I’m checking the final sample and character state.

The 30-minute run peaked at **3,229 normalized Hitpoints XP/min**. The tracker recorded **161,428 raw XP** in the fixed 15-second window from **29:15 to 29:30**, when I turned in Witch’s House and immediately fought nearby druids.

Earlier combat peaks were **63 XP/min** on cows and **106 XP/min** on deadly red spiders. The character respawned twice and finished in Lumbridge at **77 Hitpoints**, up from level 20, with **213,927 raw Hitpoints XP gained**.
I’ll check the character’s state, skip the tutorial, and get a Thieving sample before comparing training methods.
The tracker recorded a baseline of 228 real-game XP/min from pickpocketing men in Lumbridge. The character reached level 47, and I’m moving to Ardougne to test higher-XP targets with food nearby.
The character reached level 99. Knights have produced a verified 3,077 XP/min window. I’m also testing heroes and a quest that can award two Thieving XP rewards in the same 15-second window.

I’ve trained the Smithing and Fletching requirements for The Tourist Trap. A death in the mining camp cost the first set of supplies. I’m retrying with more food and checking that the disguise is equipped before entering the mine. The verified peak remains 3,077 XP/min.

The Tourist Trap and the follow-up warrior pickpockets raised the verified peak to 3,300 XP/min. The two quest rewards landed on opposite sides of a sample boundary. I’m using the remaining time for another knight run at level 99.

**Verified peak: 4,088 real-game Thieving XP/min.** Pickpocketing Knights of Ardougne at level 99 earned 204,427 raw XP in the fixed 15-second window from **29:15 to 29:30**.

The Lumbridge baseline was 228 XP/min. The Tourist Trap rewards landed in separate samples, and the better window reached 3,300 XP/min with follow-up warrior pickpockets.

The 30-minute benchmark is complete. The character finished at **99 Thieving with 2,456,612 raw XP**.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip and a single chop, then use the fixed 15-second samples to compare training approaches over the 30 minutes.

The tracker recorded 206 normalized XP/min on oaks with the bronze axe. I’m selling the logs to buy a steel axe, then I’ll compare higher-tier trees and test the Woodcutting reward from Monk’s Friend.
Willows reached 776 normalized XP/min after I let each tree keep producing logs until it fell. Monk’s Friend is ready to turn in. I’m testing magic trees and maples before using that one-time reward.
The mithril axe I forged pushed the chopping-only peak to 1,050 normalized XP/min on maples. I’ll use the remaining samples to test willows with the same axe and time the quest turn-in.

**Peak score: 1,776 normalized Woodcutting XP/min.** The tracker recorded 88,813 raw XP in the final 15-second window, from 29:45 to 30:00. Monk’s Friend awarded 50,000 raw XP, and chopping willows with the mithril axe added 38,813.

The best chopping-only window was **1,181 XP/min** on willows, up from 1,050 on maples. The character finished the 30-minute run at **level 99 Woodcutting with 1,196,500 XP**.
I’ll start with one log, check the first scored window, then use the 30 minutes to test which logs and lighting rhythm give the highest peak.

The first normal log scored 20 XP/min. Burning 13 oak logs in one sampling window raised the peak to 390. I’m gathering willows in full inventories now and testing how quickly I can light them in a clear row.

Willows raised the verified peak to 810 XP/min. The character died crossing White Wolf Mountain, then recovered at Lumbridge. I bought a steel axe with proceeds from selling logs and took the ferry to reach the yew and magic trees.

All 27 magic logs fit into one 15-second window, raising the peak to 4,101 XP/min. I’m testing whether staging extra logs beside the fire line lets the character burn more than one inventory before the window closes.

The shorter pickup worked. With five spare magic logs staged on the line, 31 fires counted in one window for a verified 4,709 XP/min. Firemaking is now level 97, and I’m testing the final runs at the higher level.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, check what the character has, and get a Crafting XP sample before comparing faster methods.
Spinning wool in Lumbridge gave the first scored window. I’m using the wool for Sheep Shearer, then targeting Elemental Workshop’s 5,000 base Crafting XP reward for a larger burst.

Sheep Shearer raised Crafting to level 25. The character died crossing White Wolf Mountain, so I replaced the lost supplies and took the ferry through Karamja. The Mining and Smithing requirements are now met, and I have the workshop key.
The elemental metal is ready, and I’ve matched Frank’s fingerprints to the dagger. I’m timing the Murder Mystery turn-in and the final workshop action to land in the same 15-second sample.

The tracker confirmed **3,203 normalized Crafting XP/min**. Both rewards landed about nine seconds apart, putting 160,150 raw XP in one sample. I’m using the remaining time to train with flax at Seers’ Village.

**Peak score: 3,203 real-game Crafting XP/min** over the completed 30-minute run.

The tracker recorded **160,150 raw XP** in the 15-second window from **27:30 to 27:45**. I turned in Murder Mystery, then finished Elemental Workshop about nine seconds later.

Crafting rose from **level 1 to level 73**, finishing at **165,212 XP**. Spinning wool and completing Sheep Shearer established a **75 XP/min** baseline. I also gathered flax, but didn’t reach the spinning wheel before time expired.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, get a Fletching sample on the board, then use the tracker to compare methods over the 30 minutes.
The tracker recorded 94 XP/min from arrow shafts and 313 XP/min from a batch of oak longbows. I’m selling the bows to fund feathers and metal arrowtips, which can be assembled in stacks of 15.

Banking the logs first let me cut 41 maple longbows in one sampling window. That raised the verified peak to 1,195 XP/min. I’ve also banked 510 arrowtips across four metals for a separate assembly test.
The tracker confirmed 4,715 XP/min. In the 29:00–29:15 window, I tipped all 1,520 arrows and cut 21 yew longbows for 235,775 raw XP. I’m finishing the session at the Edgeville yews.

**Verified peak: 4,715 real-game Fletching XP/min.** The best 15-second window ran from 29:00 to 29:15. Tipping 1,520 arrows and cutting 21 yew longbows earned **235,775 raw XP** in that window.

The full 30-minute run took Fletching from **level 1 to level 90**, finishing at **556,520 XP**. The best earlier method was batch-cutting banked maple longbows at 1,195 XP/min.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, get a Mining sample on the board, then use the tracker’s 15-second windows to compare approaches.
The tracker recorded 315 normalized XP/min on iron. I’m gathering the supplies for Doric’s Quest to test how its lump-sum Mining reward compares with a full window of ore mining.

Doric’s Quest awarded 32,500 raw Mining XP in one sample, raising the verified peak to 650 XP/min. I’m now working toward The Dig Site, which offers a larger Mining reward and has three skill prerequisites.

The character now meets all three Dig Site requirements with 41 Thieving, 28 Herblore, and 10 Agility. I’m heading to the examination centre with the digging supplies. The recorded Mining peak is still 650 XP/min.

**Peak Mining rate: 650 normalized XP/min.** Doric’s Quest awarded 32,500 raw Mining XP in the 15-second window from 6:15 to 6:30. Iron mining peaked at 333 normalized XP/min.

The character finished the 30-minute run at **Mining level 66 with 103,287 XP**, up from level 1. I passed all three Dig Site exams and unlocked the private shafts, but the quest reward was still pending when time expired.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, get a Prayer XP sample, then use the fixed-window score to compare training methods over the 30 minutes.
Burying one set of bones established a baseline of 2 normalized XP/min. I’m working through The Restless Ghost, then aiming for Holy Grail’s larger single Prayer reward.

The Restless Ghost raised the verified peak to 562 XP/min. Sir Mordred defeated the character on the first attempt. I’ve since raised Attack to 32 and Strength to 37, gathered food, and returned for the fight.
Merlin’s Crystal is complete. The character has Excalibur and both magic whistles, and is on the way to the Black Knight Titan. The verified peak is still 562 XP/min.
The Black Knight Titan defeated the character before I could claim Holy Grail’s reward. I’ve switched to collecting and burying big bones in the Wilderness for the remaining time.

**Peak Prayer rate: 562 normalized XP/min.** Completing *The Restless Ghost* awarded 28,125 raw XP in the fixed 15-second window from **5:00 to 5:15**.

The character finished the 30-minute run at **Prayer level 49 with 31,612 XP**, up from level 1. I also tested regular bones and Wilderness big bones. I completed *Merlin’s Crystal* and reached the Black Knight Titan, but lost the fight before earning *Holy Grail*’s Prayer reward.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, establish a Defence XP baseline, then compare training methods against the fixed 15-second samples.
The first sword fight registered 14 normalized Defence XP/min. I’m working toward the Holy Grail reward because its Defence XP lands in a single sampling window.
Sir Mordred defeated the character on the first attempt. I completed The Restless Ghost during recovery, which raised Prayer to 47 and unlocked Protect from Melee for the rematch.

The steel sword raised the measured peak to 130 XP/min on cows. With roughly four minutes left and the Holy Grail still several trips away, I’m switching to sustained melee on higher-HP targets to improve that score.

Rock crabs pushed the peak to 438 normalized Defence XP/min. Excalibur’s defensive Block style earned 21,900 raw Defence XP in one fixed 15-second window. I’m keeping that setup through the final samples.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, then get a Strength XP sample and use the fixed 15-second readings to compare training approaches.

The tracker recorded 16 normalized Strength XP/min from the first fight. I’m trying the Waterfall Quest next. Its 13,750 Strength XP reward lands in one action, which makes it a good candidate for the peak window.
The bot crossed the waterfall and recovered the Book on Baxtorian. I’ve banked the weapons and runes for Glarial’s Tomb and am heading to the gnome dungeon for the pebble that opens it.

The bot found the dungeon key and retained it after a respawn. The best combat window is now 38 XP/min. I’m restocking food before returning to Golrie so the bot can heal while moving through the dungeon.
The bot recovered Glarial’s urn and amulet and got out of the tomb. I’m taking the six sets of runes to the waterfall chamber for the quest reward.

A skeleton killed the bot after it collected the waterfall dungeon key. There’s too little time left to recover the quest items, so I’m using the remaining windows for continuous melee against Lumbridge cows.

**Peak score: 272 normalized Strength XP/min.** The tracker recorded 13,600 raw Strength XP in the 15-second window from 29:30 to 29:45 while fighting Al-Kharid warriors.

Strength rose from **level 10 to 65**, gaining **97,300 raw XP** over the 30 minutes. Lumbridge cows peaked at 218 XP/min. The Waterfall Quest attempt ended before the reward.
I’ll start fishing as soon as the character is through the tutorial, then use the 15-second samples to compare methods over the 30-minute run.

Netting shrimp and anchovies reached level 35 and recorded an 85 XP/min peak. I sold the catch for a harpoon and lobster pot. I’m also pursuing Sea Slug because its Fishing XP reward can land entirely within one scoring window.

Harpooning tuna raised the peak to 200 XP/min. I’ve rescued Kennith and left the Sea Slug reward unclaimed while I work on Fishing Contest. The trip between the two reward NPCs took 12.3 seconds in a trial, so both rewards may fit in one 15-second sample.

Sea Slug scored **3,587 XP/min** in one window. Its reward registered one dialogue step earlier than I expected, so Fishing Contest landed in a later sample. Both quests are complete. I’m using the remaining time to compare sharks, swordfish and tuna, and lobsters at Catherby.

**Peak score: 3,587 normalized Fishing XP/min.** Sea Slug awarded 179,375 raw XP in the 15-second window from 24:00 to 24:15. Fishing Contest paid out in a separate window.

The best window from catching fish was **675 XP/min**, from 15 lobsters at Catherby in the final 15 seconds.

Fishing went from **level 1 to 93**, finishing the 30-minute benchmark with **676,557 XP**.
I’ll check the character, skip the tutorial, and get a Ranged baseline before comparing training methods against the 15-second sampler.

The starter shortbow got Ranged from level 1 to 32. Rapid fire on cows raised the measured peak from 14 to 48 XP/min. I’ll test higher-hitpoint targets to see how much of each window was going into finding the next cow.
The peak reached 76 XP/min. Two deaths cost the character arrows, so I’ve restocked food and ammunition for a longer test on rock crabs, which have 50 hitpoints and can be fought in a cluster.
Rock crabs raised the peak to 596 XP/min with the oak shortbow. I’ve returned with a willow shortbow and mithril arrows and will use the last few minutes to measure the upgrade on the same targets.

**Peak score: 804 real-game Ranged XP/min.** The tracker recorded 40,200 raw XP in the 15-second window from 27:45 to 28:00.

The best window came from firing a willow shortbow on Rapid with mithril arrows at rock crabs. The earlier oak shortbow and bronze arrows peaked at 596 XP/min on the same targets.

The 30-minute run finished at **Ranged level 94**, up from level 1, with **719,300 total Ranged XP**.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, get an Attack XP sample, then compare training methods against the fixed 15-second score.

The bronze sword took Attack from level 10 to 14. I’ve collected the elemental runes for Waterfall Quest. Its 13,750 base Attack XP reward lands in one action, which makes it worth testing against the combat baseline.

Cow training raised the measured peak to 186 XP/min and brought Hitpoints to 45. Two earlier trips west ended in deaths, so I’m using the stronger character to complete Vampire Slayer before returning to Waterfall Quest.

Vampire Slayer raised the verified peak to **2,418 XP/min**. The tracker counted 120,875 raw Attack XP in one 15-second window, and the character reached Attack level 72. The Waterfall runes are banked for the dungeon.
Waterfall Quest raised the peak to **6,875 XP/min**. All 343,750 raw Attack XP landed in one fixed 15-second window. I’m using the remaining time to pursue The Grand Tree’s larger reward.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, then cook the first available ingredient to establish a baseline before testing faster methods.
Shrimp and anchovies established a 225 XP/min peak in Draynor. I’m moving to Catherby to test tuna and swordfish, then compare cooking a fresh catch with cooking from banked stock.

The Catherby range raised the peak to 550 XP/min with the first tuna and swordfish catch. White wolves interrupted the overland trip, so I reached Catherby by ferry through Karamja and Ardougne. I’m now testing how quickly the range accepts the next fish.

Timing a full inventory to the sampling clock raised the peak to **1,630 XP/min**. All 27 tuna and swordfish cooked successfully, earning 81,500 raw XP in one window. Cooking is now level 81, and the bot has started catching sharks.

Banking a second load of sharks raised the peak to **3,465 XP/min**. Both loads fit in one 15-second window. The bot reached Cooking 90, and I’m testing whether a fire beside the bank can shorten the refill.

The fire test reached **4,095 XP/min**. The fire went out during the first load, so the bot finished at the range. I’m using the permanent range for the final banked run to keep both loads on schedule.

The tracker recorded **5,145 XP/min**, and Cooking reached level 99. The winning window included 49 successfully cooked sharks. I’m finishing the remaining time and will verify the final score when the tracker closes.

**Verified peak: 5,145 real-game Cooking XP/min.** The bot cooked 49 sharks for **257,250 raw XP** in the fixed 15-second window from **29:00 to 29:15**.

The fastest method was to bank raw sharks in Catherby, start cooking at the nearby range just as a sampling window opened, and refill once during that window. The bank-side fire peaked at 4,095 XP/min and went out mid-load.

The 30-minute run finished at **Cooking 99 with 1,131,000 XP**, up from level 1.
